answer_text:
For each fixed \(x \in [0,1)\),

\[
x^n \to 0 \quad \text{as } n \to \infty,
\]

so

\[
\frac{1}{x^n+1} \to 1.
\]

At \(x=1\), the integrand is \(1/2\), but this single point does not affect the integral.

Since

\[
0 \le \frac{1}{x^n+1} \le 1
\]

for all \(x \in [0,1]\) and all \(n\), the integrands are dominated by the integrable function \(1\). By the dominated convergence theorem,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} \int_0^1 \frac{dx}{x^n+1}
=
\int_0^1 \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{x^n+1}\,dx
=
\int_0^1 1\,dx
=
1.
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
